Zod types don't override toString(), so both keys become the literal string "[object Object]" (the second overriding the first), and zod's default 'strip' unknownKeys mode drops all other properties (expiry_date, expires_in, refresh_token) from parsed data. In sync mode, this means refreshed credentials lose their expiry (e.g. googleCredentials.expiry_date = token.expiry_date would be undefined) and the refresh_token fallback is hardcoded to "refresh_token". adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is defined with computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`, which at runtime evaluate to the string representation of the Zod schema objects (effectively `"[object Object]"`), not a catch-all/index signature. This means the schema does *not* actually accept arbitrary numeric expiry fields like `expiry_date`/`expires_in`, and Zod will strip unknown keys by default. Under the `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` branch, this can prevent expiry fields from being retained/validated as intended, and can lead to repeated refreshes or outright parse failures.
